title: Interest rate risk on Bauspar and mortgage books, including §489 BGB
summary: Ongoing quantitative modelling and management of interest rate risk in a fixed-income portfolio and in building-society savings products. Valuation and hedging models for mortgage loans, Bauspar contracts and interest rate swaps, ALM-based hedging strategies, and scenario analysis for regulatory and internal reporting. Includes modelling the statutory early-termination right under §489 BGB as economic refinancing behaviour of customers under interest rate shocks.
evidence: §489 BGB grants the borrower, not the lender, a statutory right to terminate a fixed-rate loan; it is modelled as customer refinancing behaviour under rate shocks
valuation and hedging models cover mortgage loans, Bauspar contracts and interest rate swaps
ALM-based hedging strategies feed both regulatory and internal risk reporting
the rational-exercise rule and the forward-par-rate rule agree at every shock tested, with indifference at −36.17 BP
at a −50 BP shock the customer already terminates, four-fifths of the way from no shock to −100 BP
notes: Harvested from the CV, which records outcomes and no friction. Distinct from bgb-498-consumer-credit: §489 is the borrower's option, §498 the lender's remedy on default. The CV does not claim a hazard-rate formulation, so none is recorded here; that gap is what the Efron bridge proposes, not something already done. The workshop record establishes the rational-exercise threshold; what remains unmodelled is the roughly 20% of borrowers who do not follow it.
